analysis.research_question_and_background: Finite therapy resulting in sustained hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) loss for patients with chronic HBV infection (CHB) is an important therapeutic goal. In patients with HBeAg-negative infection, nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) withdrawal may achieve HBsAg loss in 5-20% of patients after 3 years.
analysis.study_design_and_population: NUC-B was a randomised, multi-centre trial in NA-treated non-cirrhotic HBeAg negative patients with CHB. 156 patients, 82 to control arm and 74 to PEG-IFNa arm, were recruited between 2017 and 2021; median age 45 years, 24% female, HBV Genotypes -A 16%, B 6%, C 4%, D 24%, E 22%, other 1%, unknown 26%.
analysis.methods: Patients were allocated to either NA withdrawal alone (control) or NA withdrawal followed by a 16 week course of PEG-IFNa 180ug weekly commencing 4 weeks after NA cessation (PEG-IFNa). The primary endpoint was HBsAg loss at 3 years.
analysis.main_results: At 3 years 3% of patients in the control arm and 14% of patients in the PEG-IFNa arm lost HBsAg (odds ratio 5.39; 95% confidence interval, (1.11, 26.19); p=0.037). In the control arm 34.9% of patients returned to NA therapy compared to 28.4% in the PEG_IFNa- arm. Exaggerated flares occurred in 27.9% of patients in the control arm compared with 13.4% in the PEG-IFNa arm.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The use of adjuvant PEG-IFNa therapy after withdrawal of NA therapy increases the rate of HBsAg loss whilst simultaneously reducing the number of exaggerated flares.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that adding PEG-IFNa to NA withdrawal may improve treatment outcomes for HBeAg-negative CHB patients by increasing HBsAg loss and reducing liver flares.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The target recruitment of 240 patients was not achieved, limiting the statistical power. The evidence strength is moderate due to the underpowered trial but the significant odds ratio and consistent secondary outcomes support the conclusion.

analysis.summary_en: The NUC-B trial investigated whether adding pegylated interferon (PEG-IFNa) to nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) withdrawal improves outcomes in HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients. In this randomized multi-center study, 156 patients were assigned to NA withdrawal alone or NA withdrawal followed by 16 weeks of PEG-IFNa. At 3 years, 14% of the PEG-IFNa group achieved HBsAg loss compared to 3% in the control group (OR 5.39; 95% CI 1.11-26.19; p=0.037). The PEG-IFNa group also had fewer exaggerated flares (13.4% vs 27.9%) and similar rates of returning to NA therapy. The study suggests that adjuvant PEG-IFNa after NA withdrawal significantly increases HBsAg loss while reducing liver flares, though the trial was underpowered with only 156 of 240 planned patients recruited.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nucleos(t)ide analog (NA) therapy suppresses hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA, but residual hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk persists. O-glycosylated hepatitis B surface antigen glycan isomer (HBsAgGi) uniquely reflects virion burden.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We evaluated the impact of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) versus entecavir (ETV) on 48-week HBsAgGi kinetics and its utility in stratifying HCC risk in 90 NA-naïve patients (ETV: 73; TAF: 17).
analysis.methods: As the assay targets genotype C-specific O-glycosylation, the findings cannot be generalised to genotypes A, B, or D. A favourable response was defined as a reduction or maintenance of low HBsAgGi levels.
analysis.main_results: TAF independently predicted a favourable response compared with ETV (penalised odds ratio 3.60, p = 0.030). In HBeAg-positive patients, a poor response was associated with increased HCC risk (hazard ratio 7.34, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.96-20.35, p = 0.001); however, the exact magnitude warrants cautious interpretation due to wide CIs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In conclusion, on-treatment HBsAgGi response is a specific surrogate marker for stratifying residual HCC risk in HBeAg-positive patients, and TAF is more effective than ETV in inducing these favourable kinetics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Adding HBsAgGi response to the aMAP score improved long-term HCC prediction exclusively in the HBeAg-positive cohort. A significant interaction occurred between HBeAg status and HBsAgGi response in relation to HCC development (p = 0.038).
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific design limitations, bias, confounding, or generalisability beyond genotype C. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited sample size and wide confidence intervals.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the impact of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) versus entecavir (ETV) on HBsAgGi kinetics and its utility in stratifying HCC risk in 90 NA-naïve patients. TAF independently predicted a favourable response compared with ETV, and in HBeAg-positive patients, a poor response was associated with increased HCC risk. Adding HBsAgGi response to the aMAP score improved long-term HCC prediction exclusively in the HBeAg-positive cohort. The findings are specific to genotype C and cannot be generalised to other genotypes.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) is a global health concern and the leading cause of chronic liver disease, including liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Limited literature exists regarding couple testing and outcomes, particularly in Northern Uganda.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Between 1st December 2023 and 28th February 2024, a hospital-based, cross-sectional study was conducted among eligible pregnant women and their male partners attending ANC of GRRH, Gulu, Uganda.
analysis.methods: Following systematic random sampling, a pretested questionnaire was administered by an interviewer. Blood samples were collected for HBV surface antigen (HBsAg) rapid test, which was performed according to manufacturer's instructions. Qualitative data was analysed using logistic regression in STATA version 15 SE.
analysis.main_results: A total of 242 couple pairs were enrolled. Overall, 8.3% (n=40) participants were seropositive for HBsAg; Male partners [M] (10.7%, n=26) and pregnant women [F] (5.8%, n=14). Factors associated with positive HBsAg were being male (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 2.45, 95% Confidence Interval [CI], 1.15 - 5.21, p=0.02), daily alcohol consumption (aOR: 4.73, 95% CI: 1.40 -16.04, p=0.01), and no prior vaccination against HBV (aOR: 12.01, 95% CI: 4.07 - 35.65, p<0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: There is a high HBsAg seropositivity rate, particularly among male partners of pregnant women. The study highlights the urgent need to strengthen and sensitise young people for premarital HBV screening.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for couples attending antenatal care to be screened for HBV, which can help in early detection and prevention of transmission. This supports the Uganda Ministry of Health's recommendation for HBV screening during antenatal care.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a single hospital setting, which may limit generalisability. The evidence strength is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and potential selection bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study determined HBV seroprevalence among heterosexual couples attending antenatal care at Gulu Regional Referral Hospital, Uganda. A cross-sectional design was used with 242 couple pairs enrolled. Overall, 8.3% of participants were HBsAg seropositive, with higher rates in male partners (10.7%) compared to pregnant women (5.8%). Factors associated with positivity included male gender, daily alcohol consumption, and lack of prior HBV vaccination. The study highlights a high seropositivity rate, particularly among male partners, and underscores the need for couple-based HBV screening during antenatal care to enhance early detection and prevention efforts.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed to evaluate the potential impact of replacing universal hepatitis B birth-dose vaccination with a targeted recommendation on neonatal and chronic HBV infections in the US, given the ACIP's 2025 decision to change the policy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A compartmental model simulated a US birth cohort of 3,659,289 infants under two vaccine recommendations: universal birth-dose vaccination and targeted birth-dose vaccination, with parameter values derived from literature and uncertainty incorporated across 5,000 iterations.
analysis.methods: The model compared outcomes under universal versus targeted birth-dose vaccination recommendations, using maternal HBV screening rates and birth-dose vaccination coverage among infants of unscreened mothers as key variables.
analysis.main_results: With an 86% maternal screening rate, universal birth-dose vaccination resulted in a median of 1,292 neonatal infections (95% PI, 670-2,228), while the targeted recommendation was associated with 628 additional neonatal infections (95% PI, 340-1,034) at 10% coverage and 69 additional infections (95% PI, -32 to 190) at 80% coverage among infants of unscreened mothers.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the targeted birth-dose vaccine recommendation will likely increase neonatal infections unless maternal screening rises substantially or vaccination coverage among infants of unscreened mothers exceeds current levels, highlighting the continued importance of universal screening and vaccination as complementary safeguards.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform policy decisions by suggesting that removing universal birth-dose vaccination could lead to increased HBV infections unless accompanied by substantial improvements in maternal screening or vaccination coverage, emphasizing the need for careful consideration of alternative safeguards.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on a compartmental model with parameter uncertainty, though the large sample size and extensive iterations provide robust estimates; limitations include the assumption that historical coverage trends will continue and the potential for unmodeled real-world factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the impact of replacing universal hepatitis B birth-dose vaccination with a targeted recommendation in the US. Using a compartmental model simulating a birth cohort of 3,659,289 infants, the researchers found that the targeted policy would likely increase neonatal HBV infections unless maternal screening rates rise substantially or vaccination coverage among infants of unscreened mothers exceeds current levels. With an 86% maternal screening rate, universal vaccination prevented a median of 1,292 neonatal infections, while the targeted approach could lead to hundreds more infections depending on coverage rates. The study underscores the importance of universal screening and vaccination as complementary safeguards against HBV transmission.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify factors contributing to hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) clearance in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection and to determine its influence on long-term prognosis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective open cohort study of 453 patients with CHB infection was conducted in the Liver Unit of two hospitals in Málaga, Spain, between 1991 and 2022. The incidence of HBsAg clearance was 1.96 cases per 100 patient-years.
analysis.methods: A multivariate Cox regression analysis was used to identify factors associated with HBsAg clearance. The impact of clearance on long-term prognosis was evaluated using a combined prognostic endpoint: need for liver transplantation, liver complications, or liver-related mortality.
analysis.main_results: HBsAg clearance was associated with a better long-term hepatic prognosis. Independent factors associated with clearance included age at first assessment over 40 years, baseline HBV DNA levels below 3.3 log10 (< 2000 IU/mL), and loss of hepatitis B e-antigen (HBeAg) during follow-up.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that HBsAg clearance is linked to improved long-term outcomes in chronic hepatitis B patients, highlighting specific demographic and virological factors that may influence this clearance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the surveillance and management of chronic hepatitis B patients, particularly in identifying those at higher risk for HBsAg clearance and its associated benefits for long-term prognosis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design and potential confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and long follow-up period.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated factors associated with hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) clearance in a Spanish cohort of chronic hepatitis B patients and its impact on long-term prognosis. A prospective open cohort study of 453 patients with chronic hepatitis B infection was conducted between 1991 and 2022 in Málaga, Spain. Multivariate Cox regression analysis identified independent factors linked to HBsAg clearance, including age over 40 years, baseline HBV DNA levels below 3.3 log10, and loss of HBeAg during follow-up. The results showed that HBsAg clearance was associated with a better long-term hepatic prognosis. The study's findings have implications for understanding the natural history of chronic hepatitis B and could guide clinical management and surveillance strategies. However, the observational design and potential confounding factors limit the strength of the conclusions, though the evidence is considered moderate due to the large sample size and extended follow-up period.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review examines the long-term clinical outcomes of kidney transplantation from hepatitis B surface antigen-positive (HBsAg+) donors to HBsAg-negative recipients, focusing on infection risk, organ function, and survival outcomes.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review and meta-analysis of real-world studies, searching five databases through August 20, 2023, with 16 studies included. Incidence was reported with 95% confidence intervals, and risk factors and survival were assessed using odds ratios and hazard ratios.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HBsAg+ kidneys can achieve acceptable long-term outcomes with appropriate antiviral prophylaxis and cautious recipient selection. Donor-derived HBV infection occurred in 3.60% of recipients, with higher risk in HBsAb-negative and HBcAb-negative recipients. Liver and kidney function at 1–3 years and 5–10-year graft and patient survival were comparable to controls.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The risk of donor-derived HBV infection requires careful assessment, particularly in recipients lacking HBsAb or HBcAb. While outcomes are generally favorable, the study highlights the need for standardized HBV prophylaxis protocols and further research on long-term infection risk in specific subpopulations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings support the cautious and selective use of HBsAg-positive kidneys in appropriately selected recipients with standardized HBV prophylaxis. Future research should focus on optimizing prophylaxis strategies and assessing long-term outcomes in high-risk recipient groups.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the long-term outcomes of kidney transplantation from HBsAg-positive donors to HBsAg-negative recipients. The study found that donor-derived HBV infection occurred in 3.60% of recipients, with higher risk in those negative for HBsAb or HBcAb. Despite this, liver and kidney function at 1–3 years and 5–10-year graft and patient survival were comparable to controls. The authors conclude that HBsAg+ kidneys can achieve acceptable outcomes with appropriate antiviral prophylaxis and careful recipient selection, supporting their cautious use in transplantation programs.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the neural mechanisms of early cognitive dysfunction in HBV-related cirrhosis, specifically focusing on subcortical functional network alterations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted involving 44 patients with HBV-related cirrhosis and 37 healthy controls using resting-state fMRI to analyze subcortical functional networks.
analysis.methods: Subcortical regions were parcellated into 50 subregions, and graph theoretical analysis along with Network-Based Statistics (NBS) were applied to examine functional connectivity.
analysis.main_results: No significant group differences were found in global or nodal topological metrics, but NBS identified a significant subnetwork comprising 8 thalamo-striatal connections (component-level P=0.0381). No correlations were observed between connectivity strength and neuropsychological scores.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that HBV-related cirrhosis is associated with selective thalamo-striatal disconnection despite preserved network topology, which may represent an early neural signature preceding overt cognitive impairment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the neural basis of cognitive dysfunction in cirrhosis, potentially aiding in early detection and monitoring of hepatic encephalopathy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by the absence of correlations between connectivity and cognitive scores, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and lack of longitudinal data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated subcortical functional network alterations in 44 patients with HBV-related cirrhosis and 37 healthy controls using resting-state fMRI. Despite no significant differences in global or nodal topological metrics, Network-Based Statistics identified a significant subnetwork of 8 thalamo-striatal connections (P=0.0381). No correlations were found between connectivity strength and neuropsychological scores. The findings suggest selective thalamo-striatal disconnection as an early neural signature in cirrhosis, potentially preceding overt cognitive impairment. This provides insights into the neural mechanisms of hepatic encephalopathy, though the cross-sectional design limits causal inferences.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Viral hepatitis is a significant global public health challenge, and hepatitis B virus (HBV) is accountable for the majority of these challenges. However, there is limited evidence on the incidence of mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) and its associated factors in Ethiopia, impacting the implementation of tailored control interventions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective observational cohort study was conducted among 110 infants born to hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg)-positive mothers from February 2023 to February 2024 in selected public health facilities in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Follow-up evaluations were conducted at birth and at 9 months post-delivery.
analysis.methods: Socio-demographic and clinical characteristics of mother-infant pairs, and laboratory investigations were assessed to determine the incidence of MTCT and associated factors. Poisson regression model with robust standard errors was employed to identify factors associated with MTCT of HBV.
analysis.main_results: The incidence of MTCT of HBV was 9(8.2%) (95% CI: 4.0–15.4%). Infants who received only pentavalent vaccination starting at 6 weeks post-delivery were at risk to MTCT of HBV than infants received HepB-BD± HBIG vaccine (P = 0.006). Maternal HBV viral load > 200,000 IU/mL (P < 0.001) was significantly associated with MTCT.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified that maternal HBV viral load > 200,000 IU/mL and delayed vaccination are significant risk factors for MTCT, providing new evidence to inform targeted interventions in Ethiopia.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that early vaccination with HepB-BD± HBIG and monitoring maternal HBV viral load > 200,000 IU/mL are essential to reduce the incidence of MTCT of HBV in Ethiopia.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to a small sample size of 110 infants in Addis Ababa, which may limit generalizability. However, the prospective cohort design and robust statistical analysis provide moderate confidence in the results.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective cohort study in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, investigated the incidence of mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) of hepatitis B virus (HBV) and its associated factors among 110 infants born to HBsAg-positive mothers. The study found an MTCT incidence of 8.2%, with maternal HBV viral load > 200,000 IU/mL and delayed vaccination (starting at 6 weeks) identified as significant risk factors. The results highlight the importance of early vaccination with HepB-BD± HBIG and monitoring high viral loads to reduce MTCT, providing valuable evidence for tailored interventions in Ethiopia.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is associated with stigma that can lead to negative self-perceptions, social isolation, discrimination, and reduced healthcare engagement. The study sought to elucidate the patient perspective of HBV-related stigma and to construct a patient-centric conceptual model of this experience.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study recruited 28 adults with confirmed chronic HBV infection from the US, China, and Poland. Semi-structured, qualitative interviews of approximately 60 minutes were conducted to explore participants' experiences of stigma.
analysis.methods: Qualitative, concept elicitation interviews were analyzed using Thematic Analysis methods, with stigma concepts categorized into domains and pre-determined stigma types. A patient-centric conceptual model was developed from the identified domains.
analysis.main_results: Internalized stigma was reported by all 28 participants (100%), social stigma by 22 participants (79%), and institutional stigma by 16 participants (57%). Seven domains were identified, with social functioning (100%), emotional wellbeing (96%), and HBV transmission (96%) most frequently reported.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted stigma experiences as highly pervasive and inter-related, with a pervasive impact on health-related quality of life. They concluded that reducing internalized stigma would be most impactful due to its high prevalence and bothersome nature.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to address internalized stigma in chronic HBV infection, which may improve patient engagement with healthcare and overall quality of life.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The small sample size (n=28) and qualitative design limit generalizability, and the study did not include participants from all HBV-endemic regions. The evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study explored the patient experience of stigma associated with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection through semi-structured interviews with 28 adults from the US, China, and Poland. All participants reported internalized stigma, 79% reported social stigma, and 57% reported institutional stigma. Seven domains of stigma were identified, with social functioning, emotional wellbeing, and HBV transmission most frequently reported. The authors concluded that stigma experiences were highly pervasive and inter-related, with a significant impact on health-related quality of life. They emphasized that reducing internalized stigma would be most impactful due to its high prevalence and bothersome nature. The study highlights the need for targeted interventions to address stigma and improve patient engagement with healthcare.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is a major public health issue globally, and this study aimed to evaluate the humoral immune response to the HBV vaccine in children with HIV and insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (IDDM).
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case-control study was conducted from May 2 to July 28, 2019, at Ayder Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, involving 90 children (30 with HIV, 30 with IDDM, and 30 healthy controls) with mean ages of 6.22 ± 3.03, 6.16 ± 2.56, and 6.37 ± 2.78 years, respectively.
analysis.methods: A five ml blood sample was collected for quantification of anti-HBs antibodies using MAGLUMI 800, with data analyzed using EPI data version 4.6 and GraphPad Prism Version 10.4.0, employing one-way ANOVA and logistic regression models to assess factors associated with protective responses.
analysis.main_results: Children with HIV and IDDM had significantly lower Anti-HBs titers compared to healthy controls, with means ± SD of 291.16 ± 362.8 versus 551.3 ± 431.5 (p = 0.014) and 276.33 ± 338.63 versus 551.3 ± 431.5 (p = 0.008), respectively, with a significant mean difference observed among groups (p = 0.009).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that a reduced anti-HBs antibody response following HBV vaccination was observed in children with HIV infection and IDDM, with younger age (≤ 5 years) and shorter time since vaccination (< 7 years) being independently associated with diminished antibody responses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest the need for regular follow-up assessments of antibody levels and large-scale investigations for improved monitoring and control of HBV vaccination in children with HIV and IDDM.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its small sample size and single-center design, but the evidence strength is moderate due to the controlled case-control design and statistically significant results.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the humoral immune response to hepatitis B vaccination in children with HIV and type 1 diabetes mellitus (IDDM) compared to healthy controls. A case-control study conducted in Ethiopia found that children with HIV and IDDM had significantly lower anti-HBs antibody titers than healthy controls, with younger age and shorter time since vaccination being associated with diminished responses. The findings highlight the need for regular monitoring of antibody levels in these high-risk groups to ensure adequate protection against HBV infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis Delta Virus (HDV) infection in HBV-infected individuals is associated with severe clinical outcomes, and screening is recommended in HBsAg-positive patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study to assess anti-HDV antibodies among 46 HBsAg-positive blood donors at Fundação Pró-Sangue/Hemocentro de São Paulo, 381 patients with chronic hepatitis B from the Central Laboratory Division of HC-FMUSP, and 189 individuals from the Hepatology Clinic of HC-FMUSP (101 HIV-infected and 88 chronically HBV-infected).
analysis.methods: We used a rapid lateral flow assay (LFA) to assess anti-HDV antibodies in Brazil, where HDV is highly endemic in the North, while data from the Southeast, particularly São Paulo, remain limited. Anti-HDV antibodies were detected using a validated LFA. Positive controls (n = 24) included samples previously confirmed by ELISA and/or PCR, predominantly infected with HDV genotypes 3 and 8.
analysis.main_results: Among 443,400 blood donations, 48 (0.01%) were positive for at least two HBV markers; of these, 46 were tested for HDV, and all were anti-HDV negative. All 381 patients undergoing HBV viral load monitoring were anti-HDV negative, as were all 189 patients receiving hepatology care, including those with HIV coinfection or advanced liver disease.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The absence of detectable anti-HDV among diverse at-risk populations in São Paulo is consistent with the low endemicity of HDV infection in southeastern Brazil. These findings, together with the assay's high specificity in HDV RNA-positive controls, support its potential utility as a screening tool for HDV infection in low-prevalence settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides valuable data on HDV prevalence in a low-endemicity region, informing screening strategies and resource allocation for HDV infection in HBV-positive populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was retrospective and cross-sectional, limiting causal inference. The evidence strength is moderate due to the large sample size and validated assay, but the findings may not generalize to other regions with different HDV endemicity.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the prevalence of Hepatitis Delta Virus (HDV) infection among HBsAg-positive blood donors, HIV-infected individuals, and patients with chronic hepatitis B in São Paulo, Brazil, using a rapid lateral flow assay. The retrospective cross-sectional study included 46 HBsAg-positive blood donors, 381 chronic hepatitis B patients, and 189 individuals from a hepatology clinic (101 HIV-infected and 88 chronically HBV-infected). All tested samples were negative for anti-HDV antibodies, consistent with low HDV endemicity in southeastern Brazil. The validated assay showed high specificity in HDV RNA-positive controls, supporting its utility as a screening tool in low-prevalence settings. The findings provide valuable data for HDV screening strategies in HBV-positive populations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus remains a major global public health concern, responsible for significant morbidity and mortality due to complications such as chronic hepatitis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Medical students are particularly vulnerable to hepatitis B virus infection because of occupational exposure, including needle-stick injuries and contact with infected blood or body fluids during clinical training.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An analytical cross-sectional study was conducted from March to May 2025 among undergraduate clinical-year medical students at Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. A total of 343 students participated in the study, most of whom were aged 20-24 years (61.8%), male (65.0%), and in their fifth (final) year of study (53.4%).
analysis.methods: Data were collected using a structured questionnaire, and descriptive statistics were used to determine vaccination coverage. Regression analysis was performed using Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (International Business Machines Corporation) version 28 to identify factors associated with vaccine uptake.
analysis.main_results: Overall, 78.1% had received at least one dose of the hepatitis B vaccine, but only 42.2% had completed the full vaccination schedule. The main reason for incomplete vaccination was awaiting subsequent doses (75%). Multivariable analysis showed that female sex (adjusted odds ratio = 1.99, p = 0.014), prior information about the importance of vaccination (adjusted odds ratio = 3.35, p = 0.004), previous hepatitis B testing (adjusted odds ratio = 3.14, p < 0.001), and fear of contracting hepatitis B (adjusted odds ratio = 2.39, p = 0.028) were independently associated with vaccine uptake.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Hepatitis B virus vaccine uptake among medical students was significantly associated with vaccine awareness, perceived risk of infection, and prior hepatitis B testing, whereas scheduling conflicts, vaccine cost, and vaccine unavailability acted as barriers to vaccination. The study highlights the importance of addressing structural barriers and strengthening awareness to improve vaccination coverage.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Strengthening awareness and addressing structural barriers are important for improving vaccination coverage among medical students, who are at high risk of occupational exposure to hepatitis B virus. The findings can inform targeted interventions to enhance vaccine uptake and reduce the risk of hepatitis B infection in healthcare settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was cross-sectional, limiting the ability to establish causality. The evidence strength is moderate due to the study design and reliance on self-reported data, but the large sample size and use of multivariable analysis enhance the reliability of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study assessed hepatitis B vaccine uptake and associated factors among 343 undergraduate medical students in Tanzania. While 78.1% had received at least one dose, only 42.2% completed the full schedule. Female sex, prior vaccination information, previous hepatitis B testing, and fear of infection were significantly associated with uptake. The study highlights the need to address structural barriers and strengthen awareness to improve coverage among this high-risk group.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The pathogenesis of Hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has not been fully elucidated at present. While METTL14 is crucial in innate immunity, its specific role in HBV-related liver disease progression is unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Mouse models of HBV-related cirrhosis and HCC were established to evaluate liver injury, fibrosis, and tumorigenesis. METTL14 expression was analyzed in patient tissues and bioinformatics datasets.
analysis.methods: Mechanistic studies utilized MeRIPqPCR, RIP, and Actinomycin D assays, and hepatocyte-stellate cell co-cultures to investigate METTL14's impact on cGAS mRNA stability, the cGAS-STING pathway, and IFNB1 secretion.
analysis.main_results: METTL14 was downregulated in HBV infection, cirrhosis, and HCC. METTL14 knockdown aggravated liver injury, fibrosis, and tumor formation in mice. Mechanistic studies revealed that METTL14 overexpression in HBV-infected hepatocytes promoted the degradation of cGAS mRNA by increasing its m6A modification, thereby suppressing the cGAS-STING pathway activation and IFNB1 release.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Consequently, METTL14 overexpression inhibited stellate cell activation, which was reversed by cGAS-STING agonists. Downregulation of METTL14 reduces the degradation of cGAS mRNA through m6A modification, facilitates the cGAS-STING pathway activation and IFNB1 release, thereby accelerating HBV-related cirrhosis and HCC progressions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting the METTL14-cGAS-STING pathway could be a novel therapeutic strategy for preventing or treating HBV-related cirrhosis and HCC. This research provides new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying HBV disease progression.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in mouse models and patient tissues, but the generalizability to human populations requires further validation. The evidence strength is moderate due to the combination of in vitro and in vivo data, but additional clinical studies are needed to confirm the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of METTL14 in HBV-related cirrhosis and HCC. The researchers found that METTL14 is downregulated in HBV infection, cirrhosis, and HCC, and its knockdown exacerbates liver injury and tumor formation in mouse models. Mechanistically, METTL14 promotes the degradation of cGAS mRNA via m6A modification, suppressing the cGAS-STING pathway and IFNB1 release, which in turn inhibits stellate cell activation. These findings suggest that targeting the METTL14-cGAS-STING pathway could be a novel therapeutic strategy for HBV-related liver diseases.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The aim of this study was to determine the difference in seroprotection between fully and partially vaccinated hill tribe and stateless children aged five years in northern Thailand along with the factors associated with the absence of anti-HBs in these children since vaccine implementation began in 1992.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case–control study was conducted to collect information from hill tribe and stateless individuals living in villages in Mae Fah Luang District, Chiang Rai Province. Children with no prior immunization, delayed immunization, or incomplete hepatitis B vaccination were included as cases, while children who were completely vaccinated were included as controls. A total of 188 cases and 188 controls were included in the study; 54% were male, and 54.3% belonged to the Akha group.
analysis.methods: A questionnaire was distributed and 3 mL blood samples were collected for the qualitative and quantitative detection of hepatitis B biomarkers. Logistic regression was applied to detect factors associated with the absence of anti-HBs.
analysis.main_results: The overall prevalence of anti-HBs was 59.3%; 55.3% of anti-HBs was detected in children with complete vaccination (with 2 children positive for anti-HBc), and 55.3% was detected in children with incomplete vaccination. Children whose birth weight was <2500 g (AOR = 3.52; 95% CI = 1.39–9.12), whose mother belonged to the Yao group (AOR = 16.90; 95% CI = 2.00–142.57), whose mother practiced Christianity (AOR = 2.30; 95% CI = 1.18–4.46), and whose father was aged 30–39 years (AOR = 2.20; 95% CI = 1.01–4.80) were more likely to exhibit an absence of anti-HBs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The hepatitis B vaccine-induced immune response rate among hill tribe and stateless children remains undesirable, and an effective assessment program is needed to monitor this issue.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve hepatitis B vaccine coverage and immune response in vulnerable populations such as hill tribe and stateless children in northern Thailand.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to a specific population in northern Thailand, which may affect generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate due to the case-control design and the inclusion of both complete and incomplete vaccination groups.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated seroprotection differences between fully and partially vaccinated hill tribe and stateless children in northern Thailand. A case-control study included 188 cases (incompletely vaccinated) and 188 controls (fully vaccinated), with 54% male and 54.3% Akha ethnicity. Anti-HBs prevalence was 59.3%, with 55.3% in both complete and incomplete vaccination groups. Factors associated with anti-HBs absence included low birth weight (<2500 g), maternal Yao ethnicity, maternal Christianity, and paternal age 30–39 years. The study highlights the need for improved vaccine monitoring in this vulnerable population.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) remains a significant public health challenge in Iraq, necessitating a comprehensive evaluation of the national hepatitis B control plan. This study aimed to assess the epidemiological trends of HBV in Iraq from 2015 to 2022 and evaluate the implementation and effectiveness of the national control plan.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted using national HBV surveillance data from all available Iraqi governorates between 2015 and 2022. The program evaluation component was performed in Wasit Governorate and included 24 randomly selected primary health care centers (PHCCs).
analysis.methods: Descriptive statistics, Mann–Whitney U, Kruskal–Wallis, and chi-square tests were performed using SPSS version 25 and Microsoft Excel.
analysis.main_results: The annual HBV incidence rate declined from 8.3 to 3.5 per 100,000 population between 2015 and 2022, with consistently higher incidence rates among males and marked geographic variation across governorates. The highest incidence rates were observed among individuals aged 15–45 years and those aged > 45 years. Evaluation of PHCC performance showed that 88% achieved acceptable evaluation scores, although substantial variability in performance was observed across facilities.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of Iraq’s national hepatitis B control plan, demonstrating declining incidence rates alongside important demographic and geographic disparities. Although vaccination coverage has improved substantially, important gaps remain in HBV diagnosis, prevention of mother-to-child transmission, and PHCC performance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide evidence to guide targeted interventions, strengthen health service delivery, and inform future policy decisions aimed at advancing hepatitis B control in Iraq.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s cross-sectional design and reliance on surveillance data limit causal inference and may underrepresent undiagnosed or unreported cases, reducing generalisability. The evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to these limitations and the absence of detailed molecular or genotype-specific data.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated Iraq’s national hepatitis B control plan using national surveillance data from 2015 to 2022 and a program evaluation in Wasit Governorate’s 24 primary health care centers. Descriptive and comparative statistical analyses were performed to assess trends and program performance. The annual HBV incidence declined from 8.3 to 3.5 per 100,000 population, with higher rates among males and geographic disparities, and highest incidence in adults aged 15–45 and over 45 years. Childhood vaccination coverage exceeded targets, but gaps persisted in diagnosis, prevention of mother-to-child transmission, and PHCC performance variability. The findings highlight progress alongside critical service delivery gaps, offering evidence to guide targeted interventions and policy decisions for advancing HBV control in Iraq.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on sexual dysfunction (SD) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB), examining its pathophysiology, clinical burden, and integrated management across disease stages and treatment contexts.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a narrative review that synthesizes evidence on the epidemiology, clinical burden, pathophysiological mechanisms, and antiviral treatment implications of SD in CHB.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: SD in CHB is insufficiently characterized and not routinely integrated into clinical management. Mechanistically, it involves interactions among biological vulnerability, psychological stressors, and lifestyle determinants. Nucleos(t)ide analogues do not consistently adversely affect sexual function, while interferon-based regimens may indirectly contribute to SD through fatigue and neuropsychiatric symptoms.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Reported prevalence estimates vary widely (8.6 to 63.1%) across heterogeneous HBV-related studies. Evidence on treatment effects remains limited, and the mechanisms and management of SD in CHB are not well-defined.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: An integrated management framework is proposed, including proactive screening, multidimensional assessment, individualized intervention, and longitudinal monitoring. Future research should prioritize prospective longitudinal studies, sex-specific analyses, standardized sexual function instruments, and inclusion of sexual health as a patient-reported endpoint in antiviral therapy trials.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review examines sexual dysfunction (SD) in chronic hepatitis B (CHB), highlighting its insufficient characterization in clinical management. SD involves interactions between biological, psychological, and lifestyle factors. While nucleos(t)ide analogues show no consistent adverse effects on sexual function, interferon-based regimens may indirectly contribute to SD through fatigue and neuropsychiatric symptoms. The review proposes an integrated management framework with proactive screening and multidimensional assessment. Prevalence estimates vary widely (8.6-63.1%), and future research should focus on longitudinal studies, sex-specific analyses, and standardized instruments to better define SD's burden and management in CHB.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Functional cure of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a significant challenge, making viral-entry-blocking antibodies a promising antiviral strategy.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we developed a structure-guided computational workflow for affinity-enhancing candidate mutations at the interface between the humanized neutralizing antibody HzKR127 and the HBV preS1 peptide epitope.
analysis.methods: Based on the crystal structure of the HzKR127–preS1 complex, we performed single-site saturation mutagenesis across the paratope, evaluating variants with a consensus effect score integrated from seven computational models.
analysis.main_results: Benchmarking against published alanine scanning data showed that our consensus score effectively identified major-affinity-loss residues, achieving ROC AUC values of 0.81 and 0.84 for residue-level and site-level predictions, respectively.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Mutational profiling revealed distinct asymmetric mutational responses, with broad intolerance on the preS1 side and localized favorable substitutions within antibody CDRs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Multilevel prioritization identified 26 antibody-side candidates, 17 of which showed improved HADDOCK refinement scores compared to the wild type.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: In particular, the H:D97W/F/Y substitutions presented the strongest structural rationale for enhancing improved interfacial packing through aromatic hydrophobic contacts with preS1 Phe10.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a computational strategy for optimizing the preS1 epitope recognition of the humanized antibody HzKR127 against hepatitis B virus (HBV). The researchers used the crystal structure of the HzKR127–preS1 complex to perform single-site saturation mutagenesis and evaluate candidate mutations with a consensus effect score from seven models. Their results showed that the consensus score effectively identified residues affecting affinity, achieving ROC AUC values of 0.81 and 0.84 for residue-level and site-level predictions. Mutational profiling revealed asymmetric responses, with broad intolerance on the preS1 side and favorable substitutions in antibody CDRs. The study identified 26 antibody-side candidates, 17 of which improved HADDOCK refinement scores. The H:D97W/F/Y substitutions were highlighted as having strong structural rationale for enhancing interfacial packing. These findings provide a prioritized list of candidates for experimental validation and a framework for optimizing antibodies targeting HBV epitopes. The study's evidence is strong, but it is limited to computational methods and does not include experimental validation of the results.

analysis.research_question_and_background: As little is known about the disease burden of chronic hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection, this study examined health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and fatigue at different disease stages.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a real-world quantitative cross-sectional survey of patients in Germany, Italy, Spain and the USA. Patients were recruited via their treating physicians, and of 211 patients, 41% were noncirrhotic (F0-F3); 20% had liver cirrhosis with normal function (compensated); 20% had liver cirrhosis (F4) with impaired function (decompensated); 19% had hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
analysis.methods: ANOVA was used to analyze EQ-5D-3L visual analogue scale (VAS) scores and index values, Hepatitis Quality of Life Questionnaire v2 domain scores, and Fatigue Severity Scale (FSS) total scores across different disease stages.
analysis.main_results: ANOVA showed a significant decrease in EQ-5D-3L VAS scores and index values with worsening disease stage and increasing severity (all p < 0.0001). All domain scores of the Hepatitis Quality of Life Questionnaire v2 (except positive wellbeing) worsened with progressing disease and increasing symptom severity (all p ≤ 0.0001). Mean FSS total scores also increased with worsening of disease and increasing symptom severity (both p < 0.0001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: HDV infection significantly impacts patients' HRQoL and fatigue, particularly for patients at later disease stages. The study provides novel real-world evidence on the burden of HDV infection across different disease stages.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Treatments that slow disease progression, reducing the burden of HDV infection, are needed. The findings highlight the importance of monitoring and addressing HRQoL and fatigue in HDV patients, especially those with advanced disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was a cross-sectional survey, which limits causal inference. The evidence strength is moderate due to the real-world design and large sample size, but the cross-sectional nature and potential selection bias may affect generalizability.

analysis.summary_en: This real-world international study investigated the impact of chronic hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and fatigue across different disease stages. A cross-sectional survey of 211 patients in Germany, Italy, Spain, and the USA revealed significant decreases in EQ-5D-3L scores and worsening Hepatitis Quality of Life Questionnaire v2 domain scores (except positive wellbeing) with advancing disease severity. Fatigue Severity Scale scores also increased with disease progression. The study demonstrates that HDV infection significantly impairs HRQoL and fatigue, particularly in patients with advanced disease, highlighting the need for treatments that slow disease progression to reduce this burden.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the relationship between plasma albumin levels in patients with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR TB) and co-infection with hepatitis B virus (HBV).
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study examined a patient diagnosed with MDR TB and hepatitis B co-infection, with laboratory confirmation of HBV infection through HBsAg values and assessment of nutritional status via BMI.
analysis.methods: The study evaluated plasma albumin levels in a patient with confirmed MDR TB and hepatitis B co-infection, using laboratory results for HBsAg and BMI as indicators of nutritional status.
analysis.main_results: The patient had HBsAg values of 1000 and a BMI of 19.53, indicating poor nutritional intake and hypoalbuminemia associated with both MDR TB and hepatitis B co-infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors hypothesized that hypoalbuminemia in this patient was linked to liver damage from hepatitis B and malnutrition due to MDR TB, aligning with the patient's clinical presentation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of monitoring albumin levels in MDR TB patients with hepatitis B co-infection to assess nutritional status and liver function, which may impact treatment outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on a single case study, limiting generalizability, but provides specific insights into the relationship between hypoalbuminemia, MDR TB, and hepatitis B co-infection.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between plasma albumin levels in patients with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR TB) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) co-infection. The case study describes a patient with confirmed MDR TB and hepatitis B, evidenced by HBsAg values of 1000 and a BMI of 19.53, indicating poor nutritional status. Hypoalbuminemia is associated with both conditions, resulting from liver damage due to HBV and malnutrition from MDR TB. The findings suggest that monitoring albumin levels is crucial for assessing nutritional and liver health in co-infected patients, potentially informing treatment strategies. However, the evidence is limited to a single case, reducing generalizability.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) are widely used in cancer treatment, but their safety in patients with pre-existing hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains uncertain. This study evaluated HBV reactivation and HBV-related outcomes among HBV-positive cancer patients receiving ICIs.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included adult patients treated with ICIs between January 2017 and December 2022. Patients were grouped according to receipt of antiviral prophylaxis.
analysis.methods: The primary outcome was HBV reactivation during ICI therapy. Secondary outcomes included hepatic flare, severity, and timing of reactivation, response to antiviral therapy, and factors associated with HBV-related outcomes.
analysis.main_results: A total of 160 patients were included; 68 received antiviral prophylaxis and 92 did not. HBV reactivation occurred in 3 patients (1.9%) and the odd ratio between antiviral prophylaxis and HBV reactivation was wide and imprecise (2.76; 95% CI 0.25–31.05). Hepatic flare occurred in 16 patients (10.0%) and was more frequent in the prophylaxis group than in the no-prophylaxis group (19.1% vs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In this multicenter retrospective cohort study, the HBV reactivation rate was low and could not determine whether antiviral prophylaxis reduced the risk of reactivation. Hepatic flares were significantly more common among patients who received antiviral prophylaxis, likely reflecting a higher baseline risk of HBV-related complications in this group.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: A future randomized controlled trial is warranted to guide risk-adapted antiviral prophylaxis and monitoring. The findings suggest that routine antiviral prophylaxis may not be necessary for all HBV-positive cancer patients receiving ICIs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its retrospective design and small sample size, which may have affected the precision of the results. The evidence strength is moderate due to the multicenter design but limited by the lack of randomization and potential confounding factors.

analysis.summary_en: This multicenter retrospective cohort study evaluated the safety of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in 160 hepatitis B virus (HBV)-positive cancer patients between 2017 and 2022. The study found a low HBV reactivation rate of 1.9%, with no clear evidence that antiviral prophylaxis reduced reactivation risk. However, hepatic flares were more common in the prophylaxis group (19.1% vs. lower in no-prophylaxis group), suggesting higher baseline risk in prophylaxis recipients. The authors concluded that routine antiviral prophylaxis may not be necessary for all HBV-positive patients and called for future randomized controlled trials to guide risk-adapted strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the impact of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) on the antiviral efficacy of pegylated interferon-α (PegIFNα) in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and identify baseline predictors of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) clearance, addressing the controversial question of whether NAFLD affects PegIFNα treatment response.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 201 CHB patients receiving PegIFNα monotherapy or in combination with nucleos(t)ide analogs, stratified into CHB-only (n = 125) and CHB + NAFLD (n = 76) groups based on hepatic steatosis presence.
analysis.methods: Baseline clinical, virological, and histological characteristics were compared, and cumulative HBsAg clearance, biochemical response, and virological response rates were assessed using Cox proportional hazards regression models for univariable and multivariable analyses.
analysis.main_results: No significant difference was observed in the 48-week cumulative HBsAg clearance rate between the CHB + NAFLD and CHB-only groups (18.42% vs 23.2%, P = 0.41), nor in virological response rates, but the biochemical response rate was significantly lower in the CHB + NAFLD group (13.79% vs 22.03%, P = 0.042).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that concurrent NAFLD does not significantly impair HBsAg clearance rates in CHB patients receiving PegIFNα-based therapy but is associated with reduced biochemical response rates, with baseline HBsAg and HBV DNA levels serving as independent predictors of HBsAg clearance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide important clinical insights for the management of patients with both CHB and NAFLD, indicating that HBsAg clearance depends mainly on baseline viral levels rather than NAFLD presence, though NAFLD may delay biochemical marker normalization.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the retrospective cohort design, which may introduce confounding factors, though the study provides valuable real-world data on a clinically relevant population.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study investigated the impact of nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) on pegylated interferon-α (PegIFNα) therapy response in 201 chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients, stratified into CHB-only (n = 125) and CHB + NAFLD (n = 76) groups. The study found no significant difference in 48-week HBsAg clearance rates (18.42% vs 23.2%, P = 0.41) or virological response rates between groups, but the biochemical response rate was significantly lower in the CHB + NAFLD group (13.79% vs 22.03%, P = 0.042). Multivariate analysis identified baseline HBsAg and HBV DNA levels as independent predictors of HBsAg clearance, while NAFLD comorbidity was not independently associated. The findings suggest that NAFLD does not impair HBsAg clearance but may delay biochemical marker normalization, providing important clinical insights for managing coexisting CHB and NAFLD.

analysis.scope_and_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines hepatitis B virus (HBV) outcomes in people with HIV after cessation of tenofovir-containing antiretroviral therapy (ART). The central question is to estimate the risk of HBV reactivation and new HBV infection following tenofovir discontinuation in different HBV serological status groups: active HBV (HBsAg positive), resolved HBV (HBcAb positive without HBsAg), and HBV susceptibility (negative for HBsAg, HBcAb, and HBV surface antibody).
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a systematic review and meta-analysis registered with Prospero (#2025-CRD420251080460). The authors searched Medline, Embase, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane database from January 1, 2006, to February 15, 2026. They included 22 unique observational studies out of 144 abstracts and articles that underwent full-text review. A random effects model was used to calculate pooled incidence rates, and multivariable meta-regression was employed for subgroup comparisons. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2, and publication bias was tested using Egger's test.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates HBV outcomes in people with HIV after stopping tenofovir-containing ART. The study found that tenofovir-sparing ART is associated with risks of HBV reactivation and infection. For those with resolved HBV under active surveillance, the reactivation rate was 3.79/100 person-years, significantly higher than without monitoring (0.35/100 person-years). New HBV infections occurred at 1.63/100 person-years in susceptible individuals, though with very low certainty evidence. The review highlights the need for careful HBV monitoring after tenofovir cessation and calls for higher quality prospective studies to better understand these risks.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The interplay between hepatitis B virus (HBV) replication and host immunity remains poorly defined in hepatitis B-related acute-on-chronic liver failure (HBV-ACLF). analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the dynamic interplay between HBV RNA and cytokine-driven hyperinflammation in 133 HBV-ACLF patients. Non-survivors had significantly lower HBV RNA levels but higher IFN-γ levels compared to survivors, with a strong inverse correlation between these markers. Multivariate analysis identified HBV RNA and IFN-γ as independent predictors of 12-week mortality, and a combined nomogram showed superior predictive performance compared to traditional scores. The findings reveal a virus-immunity prognostic axis where declining HBV RNA paradoxically indicates a hyperinflammatory state, challenging traditional viral load-focused approaches and offering a novel tool for guiding immunomodulatory therapy.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the high burden of occult hepatitis B infection (OBI) in HIV-infected patients in southern Vietnam. The most common serological profile was susceptibility (36.4%), followed by OBI (17.4%, including 6.6% seronegative OBI) and chronic HBV (15.8%). Males and older individuals had a higher risk of chronic HBV. Genotype B predominated, but genotype C was more frequent in OBI patients. The study underscores the risk of underdiagnosis with standard serological markers and advocates for integrated molecular and serological diagnostics to improve HBV detection in high-risk populations.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection poses a persistent public health challenge among pregnant women, with regional disparities in epidemic patterns complicating efforts to prevent mother-to-child transmission (MTCT). analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study in Nanning City, China, characterized the seroepidemiology of HBV infection among 1,935 pregnant women between October 2024 and May 2025. It reported overall HBsAg seropositivity of 6.98% and identified age-dependent trends, with higher infection rates in older women and rural residents. The study highlighted suboptimal vaccination coverage and waning antibody titers over time, recommending targeted booster vaccination for childbearing-age women to reduce incident infections and vertical transmission risk. analysis.summary_en: This study identified HBV DNA ≥ 7.0 Log10 IU/mL at baseline as a significant risk factor for low-level viremia (LLV) in chronic hepatitis B patients with advanced hepatic fibrosis/compensated cirrhosis treated with tenofovir disoproxil fumarate. Among 141 patients, 17.0% developed LLV, defined as HBV DNA levels of 20-2000 IU/mL at week 48. The multivariate analysis confirmed this baseline viral load as strongly associated with LLV (OR = 18.824, P = 0.019). This finding provides a valuable prognostic indicator for clinicians managing high-risk CHB patients, potentially enabling earlier intervention to prevent disease progression and complications like hepatocellular carcinoma.

The authors highlight the importance of baseline viral titers and serial monitoring for patients with hepatitis B history receiving ICIs, though the evidence is limited to a single case.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study performed a comparative analysis involving 40 OBI blood donors and 100 healthy blood donors to evaluate clinical parameters associated with liver fibrosis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the mechanistic basis for occult hepatitis B virus infection (OBI) as a risk factor for liver fibrosis. Using a comparative design with 40 OBI blood donors and 100 healthy controls, the authors identified IL-17F as significantly upregulated in OBI through transcriptome sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells. Mechanistic experiments demonstrated that IL-17F is chiefly secreted by CD4+ T cells upon HBcAg stimulation and promotes fibrosis-related cytokine and marker expression. The findings reveal a novel pathway wherein HBcAg drives IL-17F-mediated liver fibrogenesis, offering a mechanistic explanation for OBI-associated liver disease progression. This discovery highlights IL-17F as a potential therapeutic target and supports the development of IL-17F-targeted diagnostic and anti-fibrotic interventions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed whether distinct clinical or demographic factors differentially influence 30- and 90-day hospital readmission among patients hospitalised with cirrhosis, noting uncertainty about whether the same predictors apply across these timeframes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective, multicentre, global cohort study enrolled non-electively hospitalised adult patients with cirrhosis across 125 centres in 37 countries.
analysis.methods: Variables associated with 30- and 90-day post-discharge readmission, liver transplantation, and mortality were compared using multivariable analyses to identify independent predictors.
analysis.main_results: Among 4208 patients, 47% were readmitted, 8% received liver transplantation, and 23% died within 90 days post-discharge. Country income level was significantly associated with 30- and 90-day readmission, transplantation, and mortality (all p < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that predictors of 30-day readmission also predicted 90-day readmission, highlighting disparities by country income level and the need to address health equity in cirrhosis care.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeted interventions addressing disease severity, prior ascites, prior hospitalisation, hyponatremia, and in-hospital vasopressor use could reduce early and late readmissions in hospitalised cirrhosis patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design and reliance on abstract-level evidence, which constrains causal inference and generalisability to specific healthcare settings.

analysis.summary_en: This global, multicentre, prospective cohort study of 4208 hospitalised adults with cirrhosis examined predictors of 30- and 90-day readmission, liver transplantation, and mortality. The authors found that 47% were readmitted, 8% underwent liver transplantation, and 23% died within 90 days post-discharge. Country income level was strongly associated with readmission, transplantation, and mortality. Independent predictors of higher 30- and 90-day readmissions included disease severity, prior ascites, prior hospitalisation, hyponatremia, and in-hospital vasopressor use. Prior variceal bleeding independently predicted higher 90-day readmission, while age, disease severity, mechanical ventilation, and in-hospital vasopressor use increased the odds of 30- and 90-day post-discharge death. Admission and nosocomial infections also raised the odds of 90-day mortality. The study concludes that the same variables predict both 30- and 90-day readmissions and underscores disparities by country income level, calling for equity-focused interventions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Liver cancer remains a major global health burden with high mortality and limited treatment response prediction tools. Patient-derived cancer organoids have emerged as promising preclinical models that recapitulate tumor heterogeneity; however, the biological significance of morphological diversity within established organoids remains poorly characterized in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).
analysis.study_design_and_population: We established liver cancer organoids from resected tumor tissues of 27 patients and analyzed their clinical, histological, and genomic characteristics. Organoids were classified morphologically into cystic and solid types. Organoid establishment was more frequent in older patients (>70 years), those with HBV infection, and tumors with positive beta-catenin expression.
analysis.methods: Whole exome sequencing (WES) was conducted on six matched tumor-organoid pairs to assess genomic fidelity. Associations between organoid establishment, growth characteristics, and clinical parameters were statistically evaluated. Progression-free survival (PFS) was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method and univariate Cox proportional hazards regression.
analysis.main_results: Organoids were successfully established in 13 of 27 cases (48.1%). Solid-type organoids were significantly associated with shorter PFS compared to cystic types (HR = 13.91; p = 0.0039, log-rank test). WES analysis demonstrated high concordance in somatic mutation profiles and variant allele frequency distributions between tissues and corresponding organoids.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Patient-derived liver cancer organoids preserved the genomic and histopathological features of the original tumors. Notably, solid morphology was associated with shorter PFS, suggesting that organoid growth phenotype may serve as a supplementary indicator of tumor biological behavior in HCC.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that organoid growth phenotype could potentially serve as a supplementary indicator of tumor biological behavior in HCC, aiding in treatment response prediction and clinical outcome assessment.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Given the modest cohort size and the absence of multivariate analysis, these preliminary findings should be interpreted with caution and warrant further large-scale validation. The evidence strength is moderate due to the exploratory nature and limited sample size.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether distinct organoid growth phenotypes reflect underlying tumor biology and correlate with clinical outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Liver cancer organoids were established from 27 patients and classified as cystic or solid types. Organoids were successfully established in 48.1% of cases, with solid types showing significantly shorter progression-free survival (PFS) compared to cystic types (HR = 13.91; p = 0.0039). Whole exome sequencing confirmed high genomic fidelity between tumors and organoids. The findings suggest that organoid growth phenotype may serve as a supplementary indicator of tumor biological behavior in HCC, though the modest cohort size and lack of multivariate analysis warrant further validation.

analysis.time: Published on 6-Aug-2026. The study was conducted from May 2021 to December 2024, with a 12-week treatment phase followed by a 12/48-week observational period.
analysis.location_and_population: China, with participants enrolled from thirteen centers. The study included 96 adults with chronic HBV/HCV coinfection: 77 non-cirrhotic patients (Group 1) and 19 compensated cirrhotic patients (Group 2).
analysis.event: A multicenter, prospective, single-arm, open-label trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (SOF/VEL) with pre-treatment of tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in chronic HBV/HCV coinfected patients. The study is confirmed and published in the Journal of Clinical and Translational Hepatology.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Overall sustained virologic response was 97.9% (100% in Group 2). HCV RNA, HBV DNA, and HBV RNA levels decreased significantly in all patients. Liver function markers improved, and non-invasive fibrosis indices showed modest improvement in Group 2. Two patients in Group 1 experienced HBV reactivation and HCV relapse, respectively. No drug-related adverse events were reported.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study concluded that SOF/VEL is effective with an acceptable safety profile, and pre-administration of TAF may mitigate HBV reactivation risk. The source is a full original report from EurekAlert!, published by a reputable scientific publisher (Xia & He Publishing Inc.) with peer-reviewed content.

analysis.brief_en: A recent study published in the Journal of Clinical and Translational Hepatology evaluated the safety and efficacy of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (SOF/VEL) with pre-treatment of tenofovir alafenamide fumarate (TAF) in 96 chronic HBV/HCV coinfected patients across 13 centers in China. The 12-week trial achieved a 97.9% overall sustained virologic response, with 100% in compensated cirrhotic patients. Significant improvements in liver function and fibrosis indices were observed, though two non-cirrhotic patients experienced HBV reactivation or HCV relapse. No drug-related adverse events were reported. The study suggests TAF pre-treatment may reduce HBV reactivation risk, highlighting a promising therapeutic approach for this coinfected population.

analysis.event: Researchers are developing a new therapeutic vaccine for chronic hepatitis B, aiming to train the immune system to regain control of the virus. The vaccine is intended for people already chronically infected, unlike conventional vaccines that prevent infection.

analysis.brief_en: This article discusses the development of a new therapeutic vaccine for chronic hepatitis B, part of the EU-funded TherVacB initiative. The vaccine aims to train the immune system to fight the virus, unlike traditional vaccines that prevent infection. Hepatitis B is a major global health issue, affecting around 254 million people and causing 1.1 million deaths annually, mostly from cirrhosis and liver cancer. In the EU and associated countries, approximately 3.6 million individuals are chronically infected, often unaware of their condition until serious liver damage occurs. Current antiviral treatments suppress the virus but do not eliminate it, and the virus can return after treatment stops. Early clinical trials in Germany, Italy, Spain, the UK, and Tanzania have shown the vaccine is well tolerated and stimulates the desired immune response, but its effectiveness in curing chronic hepatitis B is still under investigation. Researchers believe a functional cure may come from combining therapies that work together, rather than relying on a single treatment. The World Health Organization aims to eliminate viral hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030, which would require earlier diagnosis, broader vaccination, and more effective treatments for those already infected.

analysis.location_and_population: Northern China; population-based cohort of 3,269 adults with chronic hepatitis B virus infection.
analysis.event: A population-based cohort study reported that metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in people with chronic hepatitis B is associated with increased risks of cardiovascular disease and extrahepatic cancers, based on 13.7 years of follow-up.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: MASLD prevalence at baseline: 26.5% (867/3,269). Adjusted risk increases: 98% higher cardiovascular disease risk and 50% higher extrahepatic cancer risk. 12-year cumulative cardiovascular incidence: 9.4% with MASLD vs 4.9% without. 36 extrahepatic cancers recorded among participants with MASLD vs 69 among those without. MASLD was not independently associated with primary liver cancer after adjustment.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Study limitations include lack of longitudinal HBV DNA, antiviral treatment, and early fibrosis data; hepatic steatosis assessed by ultrasonography; findings require validation in other ethnic and lifestyle groups. Authors recommend integrating virological control and metabolic health into long-term clinical assessment and continued cardiovascular monitoring for people with chronic hepatitis B, including those with normal alanine aminotransferase or resolved hepatic steatosis.

analysis.brief_en: A population-based cohort study from northern China tracking 3,269 adults with chronic hepatitis B over 13.7 years found that metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) nearly doubled the risk of cardiovascular disease and raised extrahepatic cancer risk by 50%. Even after MASLD appeared to reverse, cardiovascular risk remained approximately twice as high. The 12-year cumulative incidence of cardiovascular events was 9.4% among participants with MASLD versus 4.9% without. The authors recommend integrating metabolic and cardiovascular monitoring into routine care for people with chronic hepatitis B, including those with normal liver enzymes or resolved steatosis, while noting study limitations such as the absence of longitudinal HBV DNA and antiviral treatment data.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a systematic review and meta-analysis that searched Medline, Global Health, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Africa Index Medicus, and the Journal of Health Science and Disease at the University of Yaounde. analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis provides updated estimates of hepatitis B virus (HBV) prevalence in Cameroon, reporting an overall pooled prevalence of 9.98% (95% CI 9.00–11.02) with high heterogeneity (I2 = 98.10%). Subgroup analyses indicate that sex, geographical area, population risk group, and study design are key sources of heterogeneity. The review highlights the urgent need for targeted interventions, especially among males and in high-prevalence regions, and calls for standardized methodologies in future prevalence studies to reduce heterogeneity and improve comparability.
